# Personal Experience

This section is focused around the personal experience of ageism of survey
participants. The answers to this question will help in our evaluation of how
ageist the IT industry is along with the Fraboni analysis.

```{r}
#| label: set-pe-Setup
#| include: false
#| echo: false

library('tidyverse')
library('ggthemes')

source("_graph_standards_bar.R")

main_df <- readRDS("main_df.rds")
```

## Vector Definitions

```{r}
#| label: vdf-pe-VectorDefinitions

# These vectors are used to be able to see the question being asked of the 
# participant.

pe_question_labels <- c(
  "Personal_Experience_1"  = "Age prevented a promotion",
  "Personal_Experience_2"  = "Age prevented receiving training",
  "Personal_Experience_3"  = "Age prevented getting a job",
  "Personal_Experience_4"  = "Excluded from groups or events due to age",
  "Personal_Experience_5"  = "Age used against me at work",
  "Personal_Experience_6"  = "Company wants me to retire soon",
  "Personal_Experience_7"  = "Harassed at work due to age",
  "Personal_Experience_8"  = "Uncomfortable at work due to age",
  "Personal_Experience_9"  = "Let go or fired due to age",
  "Personal_Experience_10" = "Challenging work given to younger employees"
)
```

## Create Personal Experience Data Frame

Create a Personal Experience data frame with ID, Age, and answers to the 10 
Personal Experience questions. Rows where more than 30% of values are missing 
are dropped — these represent respondents who skipped the section entirely. 
Remaining isolated NA values are replaced with "Neither true nor false" as a 
conservative neutral response.

```{r}
#| label: cde-pe-CreateDataFrame

personal_experience_df <- main_df |>
  select(ID, Age, starts_with("Personal_Experience_")) |>
  filter(rowMeans(is.na(across(everything()))) <= 0.3)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-pe-NACheck
#| tbl-cap: Number of Missing Values from the Personal Experience Section

personal_experience_df |>
  mutate(na_count = rowSums(is.na(across(everything())))) |>
  filter(na_count > 0) |>
  select(ID, na_count) |>
  knitr::kable(col.names = c("ID", "Num Missing"))

```

Based on this, I only have one row with NAs in them. I will update these
responses with a a neutral response.

```{r}
#| label: cde-pe-FillNAs

personal_experience_df <- personal_experience_df |>
  mutate(across(starts_with("Personal_Experience_"),
                ~replace(., is.na(.), "Neither true nor false")))
```

# Post Dataframe Manipulation Information:

Any NAs in Dataframe: ***`r anyNA(personal_experience_df)`***

Number of Research Participants for Personal Experience Analysis is: 
***`r nrow(personal_experience_df)`***

## Save Out Personal Experience Data Frame
We will be using this cleaned data frame in our Correlation Analysis.

```{r}
#| label: cde-pe-SaveDataFrame

saveRDS(personal_experience_df, 
        "personal_experience_df.rds")
```

## Summary of Reported Experiences

The following table shows the percentage of respondents who reported each
experience as True, Neutral, or False, sorted by the percentage reporting True.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-pe-Summary
#| tbl-cap: Response Distribution To Personal Experience Questions

pe_summary <- personal_experience_df |>
  select(starts_with("Personal_Experience_")) |>
  summarise(across(everything(), list(
    True    = ~round(mean(. == "True") * 100, 1),
    Neutral = ~round(mean(. == "Neither true nor false") * 100, 1),
    False   = ~round(mean(. == "False") * 100, 1)
  ))) |>
  pivot_longer(everything(),
               names_to  = c("question", "response"),
               names_sep = "_(?=True|Neutral|False)") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = response, values_from = value) |>
  mutate(label = pe_question_labels[question]) |>
  arrange(desc(True)) |>
  select(label, True, Neutral, False)

pe_summary |>
  knitr::kable(
    col.names = c("Experience", "True (%)", "Neutral (%)", "False (%)"),
    align     = c("l", "r", "r", "r")
  )
```

## Percentage Reporting True for Each Experience

```{r}
#| label: fig-pe-AgeistEncounters
#| fig-cap: |
#|  Percentage Reporting Each Ageist Experience<br>
#|  Sorted by prevalence; scale 0–100%
#| out-width: "100%"
#| fig-height: 5

pct_true_df <- pe_summary |>
  mutate(
    pct_label = paste0(True, "%"),
    label     = factor(label, levels = label[order(True)])
  )

graph_bar_chart(
  df          = pct_true_df,
  x_category  = "label",
  y_category  = "True",
  label_col   = "pct_label",
  x_label     = "Experience",
  y_label     = "% Reporting True",
  horizontal  = TRUE,
  y_limits    = c(0, 100)
)
```

The most commonly reported experience is being denied a job due to age (22.8%),
followed by promotion barriers (14.9%) and age being used against the respondent
(13.2%). Overt experiences such as harassment and termination are least common
(under 5%). This pattern suggests ageism in this sample manifests primarily 
through employment barriers rather than direct social mistreatment.

## Personal Experience by Age Group

To understand whether older IT workers experience ageism at higher rates, a 
composite experience score is computed per respondent — the count of questions 
marked "True." A higher score indicates more reported ageist experiences.

```{r}
#| label: cde-pe-PersonalExperienceByAgeGroup

pe_score_df <- personal_experience_df |>
  mutate(across(starts_with("Personal_Experience_"),
                ~case_when(. == "True" ~ 1L, TRUE ~ 0L))) |>
  mutate(exp_score = rowSums(across(starts_with("Personal_Experience_")))) |>
  select(ID, Age, exp_score)

pe_age_summary <- pe_score_df |>
  group_by(Age) |>
  summarise(
    n            = n(),
    mean_score   = round(mean(exp_score), 2),
    pct_any      = round(mean(exp_score > 0) * 100, 1),
    .groups      = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    score_label = as.character(mean_score),
    age_label   = str_remove(as.character(Age), " years old")
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-pe-PersonalExperienceGraph
#| fig-cap: |
#|  Mean Number of Ageist Experiences by Age Group<br>
#|  Count of 'True' responses out of 10 possible experiences
#| fig-height: 5
#| out-width: "100%"

graph_bar_chart(
  df          = pe_age_summary,
  x_category  = "age_label",
  y_category  = "mean_score",
  label_col   = "score_label",
  x_label     = "Respondent Age Group",
  y_label     = "Mean Experiences Reported",
  horizontal  = FALSE
)
```

```{r}
#| label: tbl-pe-AgeExperenceTable
#| tbl-cap: Age Groups and Ageist Experience

pe_age_summary |>
  select(Age, n, mean_score, pct_any) |>
  knitr::kable(
    col.names = c("Age Group", "N", "Mean Score", "% Reporting Any Experience"),
    align     = c("l", "r", "r", "r")
  )
```

## Conclusion

Respondents aged 55–64 and 65+ report the highest mean experience scores (1.23 
and 1.50 respectively) and the highest rates of reporting at least one ageist 
experience (38.5% and 37.5%). Middle-aged respondents (35–54) report 
substantially fewer experiences (mean 0.47–0.58, 23–26% reporting any). The 
youngest groups (18–34) have very small sample sizes (n=2 and n=8) and should be 
interpreted with caution.

While the focus of this paper is the impact of ageism on older IT workers, as
previously mentioned, ageism can be experienced by all age groups with higher
levels being experienced by both older and younger workers. While caution is
advised with the low sample size in the younger groups, the data is consistent
with overall expectations.

The trend among the age groups with the larger sample sizes groups (ages 35+) is 
consistent with what would be expected if age-based discrimination increases 
with age in the IT workforce. Formal statistical testing of this relationship 
will be further analyzed in the Correlations analysis Section.
